content.text: I couldn't read the source, so this diagnosis rests on the call graph and the symptom, not on the code itself.

candidates.explanation: getTokensData builds both tokens for login and refresh. `refreshToken` (line 546) calls it, and so do the login flows. A refresh token whose exp is only minutes after iat means the refresh JWT is signed with the access-token lifetime. Most likely the `expiresIn` for the refresh token reads `auth.expires` (AUTH_JWT_TOKEN_EXPIRES_IN) instead of `auth.refreshExpires` (AUTH_REFRESH_TOKEN_EXPIRES_IN). The configured 30d value is therefore ignored. The refresh token then expires with the access token, and /auth/refresh returns 401 once it has lapsed.

Secondary suspect. If the registered auth config maps `refreshExpires` to the wrong env variable (for example AUTH_JWT_TOKEN_EXPIRES_IN), the 30d setting never reaches the service. The validator would also be missing or mis-declaring AUTH_REFRESH_TOKEN_EXPIRES_IN.
Less likely. This method only passes the session id, user id and hash to getTokensData and does not set the expiry itself. It is worth checking only to confirm no expiry override happens here.

fix.description: In getTokensData, sign the refresh token with the refresh lifetime: `expiresIn: this.configService.getOrThrow('auth.refreshExpires', { infer: true })`. It currently uses the access-token lifetime (`auth.expires`). Also check that auth.config.ts maps `refreshExpires` to process.env.AUTH_REFRESH_TOKEN_EXPIRES_IN.
